learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of Prerequisites for Learning Vue in a Vue 3 application.
Apply at least one of the syllabus subtopics in a small, inspectable example.
Verify one expected behavior and identify a relevant edge case.

content.intro: This lesson studies Prerequisites for Learning Vue within Introduction to Vue.js. The source PDF subtopics are preserved below and connected to an original working-style example.
content.why_it_matters: A clear mental model helps you decide what belongs in Vue, what remains ordinary JavaScript, and when the framework is a good fit.

content_blocks.title: Prerequisites for Learning Vue: Asynchronous data workflow
content_blocks.alt_text: Asynchronous data workflow diagram for lesson 6: Prerequisites for Learning Vue. Start the request for the current input → Show pending, success, empty, or failure → Cancel stale work and display useful feedback
content_blocks.caption: Data workflow: model all request states and prevent late or failed responses from silently breaking the interface.

content_blocks.title: The idea in context
content_blocks.text: Vue is a progressive JavaScript framework for building interfaces from declarative templates, reactive state, and reusable components. This lesson focuses on Prerequisites for Learning Vue. Start by naming the state, component, browser behavior, or deployment boundary involved; then predict what should change and test the smallest example.

items.title: HTML elements and forms
items.text: For HTML elements and forms, bind the input to a clear state value, validate before submission, and associate field errors with their controls. A disabled or loading state should be reflected in the UI without treating the client as the authority for server validation.

items.title: CSS selectors, layout, and responsive design
items.text: For CSS selectors, layout, and responsive design, keep the visual rule in CSS where possible and bind reactive values only when state genuinely changes presentation. Check responsive behavior and reduced-motion preferences; animation should communicate state rather than block interaction.

items.title: JavaScript variables, functions, objects, and arrays
items.text: For JavaScript variables, functions, objects, and arrays, connect the term to a visible behavior in a small Vue 3 example. State what input or reactive dependency changes, predict the UI result, and verify the prediction with a normal case plus a boundary case.

items.title: ES modules, promises, and asynchronous JavaScript
items.text: For ES modules, promises, and asynchronous JavaScript, model pending, success, empty, and failure states. Check HTTP status before treating a response as success, cancel stale work where appropriate, and do not let a late response overwrite newer user intent.

content_blocks.expected_output: The page displays “Hello, Vue!”; changing message.value in script updates the rendered text.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Place the excerpt in App.vue in a create-vue project, run npm run dev, and open the printed local URL.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the initial values or original code, reload the development app/test, and repeat once with a boundary or failure case. Remove temporary logs and test data before committing.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Work through Prerequisites for Learning Vue with a predict–change–verify loop. First state the expected UI or console output. Change only the relevant input/state value, then observe the result. Compare it with the expected output in the code block; if it differs, check the exact file, runtime/version, browser Console, and network response before widening the investigation.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Extend the example to include “CSS selectors, layout, and responsive design”. Keep the same behavior for the ordinary input, then try an empty, invalid, repeated, or failure condition that makes sense for the example. Record the expected result before testing.

items.title: Assuming behavior instead of checking it
items.text: Write down the expected result and reproduce the issue in the smallest possible example; inspect the browser Console and the exact reactive value or request.

items.title: Ignoring an edge case
items.text: Try empty input, a missing item, repeated interaction, a failed request, or unmounting while work is pending; handle the case explicitly.

items.title: Putting every responsibility in one component
items.text: Separate display, reusable logic, API service, and shared state when that boundary makes the behavior easier to test and explain.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: Remember: Vue is a progressive JavaScript framework for building interfaces from declarative templates, reactive state, and reusable components. For Prerequisites for Learning Vue, keep the example small, verify the rendered or logged result, and consult the official references when behavior depends on a specific Vue or ecosystem version.

content_blocks.title: Accessibility, version, and runtime notes
content_blocks.text: Use semantic HTML, readable labels, keyboard-operable controls, and visible errors where the example interacts with users. Vue examples are intended for Vue 3.x with create-vue/Vite unless a legacy or specialist lesson explicitly says otherwise. This CodeLeaf playground does not execute arbitrary Vue code; the snippets are labeled for static validation and should be run in a separate local project.

content.task: Create a small example for “Prerequisites for Learning Vue” that applies “HTML elements and forms”, predicts the expected result, and verifies a relevant boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates the named Vue concept rather than only mentioning it.
The expected output or observable behavior is written down and can be checked locally.
At least one boundary, loading, invalid-input, or failure case is tested or explicitly reasoned about.
The example uses semantic/accessible interaction patterns and does not treat frontend state as authoritative security.
hints: Start with the smallest observable part of “HTML elements and forms”.
Predict the output before changing one input at a time.
Use the browser Console, Vue DevTools, or the appropriate test runner to isolate a mismatch.

common_mistakes.problem: The example only covers the happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Real interfaces receive empty values, delayed responses, invalid input, and failed requests.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one realistic edge/failure case and state its expected behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: The code assumes an API or feature exists in every runtime.
common_mistakes.why: Tool and API support depends on Vue, the build tool, or the chosen SSR/test framework.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the linked official reference and record the runtime/version assumption.

summary: Prerequisites for Learning Vue belongs to the broader area Introduction to Vue.js.
The main concept to practice is HTML elements and forms.
Verify a normal result and one meaningful boundary case before using the pattern in a production feature.
